The latest annual safety review located at this check covers 2024 and was issued on 7 August 2025.
The annual review is prepared by the CAA Safety Intelligence team using occurrence data collected under UK Regulation 376/2014.
The review includes occurrences involving UK-registered aircraft outside or inside the UK and non-UK registered aircraft occurring in the UK.
CAA states that annual-review data may change as investigations are completed.
Mandatory Occurrence Reporting has operated as part of UK aviation since 1976.
Occurrence reporting supports collection, protection, exchange and analysis of safety information for learning rather than attribution of blame or liability.
CAA lists 62,215 mandatory occurrence reports received in 2025.
CAA lists 59,750 mandatory occurrence reports received in 2024.
CAA lists 47,491 mandatory occurrence reports received in 2023.
Occurrence reports are treated confidentially to protect individual identity and maintain free reporting.
Occurrence information may be used only to maintain or improve aviation safety and is not generally released to the public or media through FOI.
Voluntary reports use the same format as mandatory reports and are triaged, prioritised, processed and analysed together.
CAA records that the ECCAIRS2 reporting endpoint changed to the ICAO-hosted reporting portal, requiring bookmark and workflow updates.
CAA guidance requires reporting wildlife and bird strikes with or without damage, including suspected strikes or flock encounters.
A UAS accident or occurrence may need to be reported to the AAIB, the CAA, or both under separate requirements.
National occurrence-report totals measure reporting activity and potential hazards and are not interpreted as local or parcel-level aviation incident rates.
